questions.question:
Which of the following temples was also called Black Pagoda by the Germanic Navinco?

A. Konark Temple

B. Jagannath Temple

C. Brahmeshwar Temple

D. Mukteshwar Temple
questions.solution:
The answer is** **__**Konark Temple.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Konark Temple was called the "Black Pagoda" in European sailor accounts because it looked like a great tiered tower that appeared black.**
 
• It is located in Konark, Puri district, Odisha.
 
• The temple was built around 1250 CE by **King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jagannath Temple:**

 
 
• Jagannath Temple in Puri was called the** "White Pagoda".**
 
• The famous **annual Ratha Yatra or chariot festival** held at Jagannath Temple.
 
• It was built in the 12th century by **Ananta Varman Chodaganga Deva, a well-known Ganga dynasty king.**
 
 
 
• Brahmeshwar Temple:
 
 
• It is a Hindu temple in **Bhubaneswar, Odisha, **dedicated to Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Mukteshwar Temple:**
 
 
• It is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva built in the 10th century in **Bhubaneswar, Odisha.**

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Ajanta Caves lie in the gorge of Waghora river.
Sanchi Stupa lies in the gorge of Chambal river.
Pandu-lena Cave Shrines lie in the gorge of Narmada river.
Amaravati Stupa lies in the gorge of Godavari river.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The **Ajanta caves **are cut into the side of a cliff that is on south side of a U-shaped gorge on the small river Waghora. ***Hence option 1 is correct.***
 
• **Sanchi Stupa **lies in an upland plateau region, on a flat-topped sandstone hill, just west of the **Betwa River **and about 5 miles (8 km) southwest of Vidisha.* **Hence option 2 is not correct.***
 
• The **Buddhist monuments Pandavleni Caves **also known by the names** Pandu Lena caves and Trirashmi caves** **are a group of 24 rock-cut caves.**
 
 
• It is l**ocated high up on the north face of Trivashmi hill 8 km south of Nasik city.**
 
• The donative inscriptions indicate that these excavations are belonging to the Satavahana and Kshatrapa periods.
 
• **The nearest river is the Godavari.* ****Hence option 3 is not correct.*
 
 
 
• **Amravati stupa **was founded by an emissary of Emperor Ashoka and its construction got completed around 2000 years ago.
 
 
• **Amravati Stupa illustrates Lord Buddha** in a human form and He is shown subduing an elephant.
 
• It is** taller than the Sanchi stupa** and has 95 ft high platforms, extending in the four cardinal directions, along with a huge circular dome.
 
• It is** situated near river Krishna. *Hence option 4 is not correct.***

questions.question: Which is the meaning of Pishtaq, an important aspect of Mughal architecture?

options.text: Central Hall surrounded by eight rooms.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__**Tall gateway**__'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There were several important architectural innovations during **Akbar’s reign.**
 
• For inspiration, Akbar’s architects turned to the tombs of his Central Asian ancestor, Timur.
 
• The central towering dome and the **tall gateway (pishtaq)** became important aspects of Mughal architecture, first visible in **Humayun’s tomb.**
 
• The tomb was placed in the centre of a huge formal chahar bagh and built in the tradition known as “**eight paradises” or hasht bihisht** – a central hall surrounded by eight rooms.
 
• 
 
The building was constructed with red sandstone, edged with white marble. 

 

Hence, we can conclude that the term Pishtaq means 'Tall gateway__'

questions.question: Which of the following rulers commissioned the Makkah Masjid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Makkah Masjid:**

 
• **Mecca Masjid Hyderabad** is one of the most beautiful mosques globally, with **huge, complex and intricate architecture.**
 
• Mecca Masjid is **located in the heart of Hyderabad.** It’s been almost a hundred years since it was first **established in the Qutab Shahi area.**
 
• This Mosque has become a **major landmark and tourist attraction in Hyderabad** because of its spiritual beauty.
 
• It is written on a stone plate in the Arabic language at the entrance of the Mosque; **It was built during the 17th century by the sixth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty**. He laid the first foundation stone of the Mecca masjid.
 
• **Muhammad Qutb Shah, the sixth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty**, **commissioned bricks to be made from the soil brought from Mecca**, the holiest site of Islam, and used them in the construction of the central arch of the mosque, **thus giving the mosque its name.**
 
• The complex was put by **UNESCO on its "tentative list" to become a World Heritage Site in 2014**.

questions.question: Which of the following temples is the example of Tri Ratha Temple Architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **Parasurameswar Temple**.

**About Ratha Temple Architecture:**

 
• **Ratha Temple-Architecture** Included the **Cutting of a Single Piece of Rock into Temple**. In this form of Architecture, the **Temples were Carved out from Top to Bottom.** 
 
• These temples are a **Facet or Vertical Offset Projection** on the plan of the **Sanctum and S****hikhara**. It is generally carried up from the **Bottom of the Temple** to the **Superstructure**. The corners of each **Ratha touch Notional Circles** on the Plan of the Temple centered on the **Idol**** Image in the Sanctum**.
 
• The **Ratha is Decorated with Geometric Statues**, such as statues of a **Gatekeeper Watching Outside** or a **Niche with a Statue** of **a Deity**. Sometimes, the **Facet of the Ratha** is **Hollowed to the Interior Surface** these are **Rathas with recesses**.
 
• If there is **only one Facet**, this is a **temple with Three Rathas (Triratha)**, **the wall, and the Facet on the Left and on the Right.**
 
• If there are the **Main Facet** and a **Secondary one**, the temple has **Five Rathas (Pancharatha)**. There are also temples with **Seven Rathas (Saptaratha), and Nine Rathas (Navaratha).**

**Image of Triratha Temple Architecture(**Parasurameswar Temple)** :**

 [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Parasurameswar_Temple.jpg/300px-Parasurameswar_Temple.jpg] 

**Notes:**

 
• Parasurameswar Temple is in the Bhubneshwar capital of Orissa. Here Lord Shiva is the deity of this temple.

questions.question: Which religion is associated with the caves of Sittanavasal?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Jain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The caves of **Sittanavasal** are associated with the **Jain religion**.
 
• Sittanavasal is a renowned archaeological site in the **Pudukkottai district** of Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• The site is famous for its **rock-cut cave temple** which dates back to the 7th century.
 
• The caves feature **beautiful frescoes and paintings** that depict Jain religious themes and motifs.
 
• These paintings are similar in style to the **Ajanta Caves** and are an important example of ancient Indian art.
 
• Sittanavasal served as a center for Jain monks and a place of meditation and worship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vaishnava**__

 __
 
• Vaishnavism is one of the major traditions within Hinduism and worships **Vishnu** and his avatars, particularly **Rama and Krishna**.
 
• Vaishnava temples often feature intricate carvings and sculptures depicting scenes from the **Ramayana and Mahabharata**.
 
 
 
• **Shaiv**__
 __
 
• Shaivism is another major tradition within Hinduism, focusing on the worship of **Shiva**.
 
• Shaiva temples are characterized by the presence of **Shivalingas** and sculptures of Nandi, the bull.
 
• Famous Shaiva sites include the **Ellora Caves** and the **Kailasa temple**.
 
 
 
• **Buddhists**__
 
 
• Buddhism is a major world religion founded by **Siddhartha Gautama**, known as the Buddha.
 
• Buddhist caves and monasteries, such as the **Ajanta and Ellora Caves**, are renowned for their detailed carvings and paintings depicting the life of the Buddha.

questions.question: Who built the Tribhuvan Narayan Temple in the Chittorgarh fort ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhoj Parmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tribhuvan Narayan Temple is located in the historic Chittorgarh Fort in Rajasthan, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• Bhoj Parmar, a renowned ruler of the Paramara dynasty, is credited with constructing the Tribhuvan Narayan Temple.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and holds significant religious and architectural importance.
 
• Bhoj Parmar was known for his patronage of art, literature, and architecture during his reign.
 
• The architectural style of the temple reflects the intricate craftsmanship prevalent during the Paramara dynasty's rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chittorgarh Fort:**

 
 
• Located in Rajasthan, Chittorgarh Fort is one of the largest forts in India and was the capital of Mewar.
 
• The fort has a rich history and is associated with legends of bravery and sacrifice, including those of Rani Padmini and Maharana Pratap.
 
• The fort houses several historical structures, including temples, palaces, and towers.
 
 
 
• **Paramara Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Paramara dynasty ruled parts of central India, primarily in present-day Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, from the 9th to the 14th century.
 
• Bhoj Parmar, one of the most famous rulers of the dynasty, is remembered for his contributions to culture and architecture.
 
• The dynasty is also associated with the promotion of Sanskrit literature and Hindu philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Temple Architecture in India:**
 
 
• Indian temples often exhibit a distinct architectural style based on the region, such as Nagara (North Indian), Dravidian (South Indian), and Vesara (mixed style).
 
• The Tribhuvan Narayan Temple reflects the Nagara style, characterized by curvilinear spires (shikhara) and detailed carvings.
 
• Such temples often served as centers of religious and social activities during historical periods.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**
 
 
• Chittorgarh Fort is part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• These forts are recognized for their unique Rajput military architecture and historical significance.

questions.question: The innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple where the idol of the main deity is placed is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Garbhagriha **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Garbhagriha

 
 
• The innermost sanctum of the Hindu temples where the idol or murti of the main deity is placed is called the Garbhagriha.
 
• It is **also called the womb chamber of the temple.**
 
• Only the **priests are allowed to enter this chamber.**
 
• The Garbhagriha is **a single chamber with the room facing towards the east to get the rising sun.**
 
• There are no windows and hardly any access to any lights.
 
• The room is a square one and the deity is normally placed at the centre for the visitors to see.
 
• The **Garbhagriha is the most important and sacred space where the deity is worshipped.**
 
• All the offerings to the deity are made inside here.

questions.question: The Vesara hybridisation and incorporation of several styles was the hallmark of which of the following dynasty?
questions.solution:
The Vesara hybridisation and incorporation of several styles was the hallmark of __**Chalukya Dynasty.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

 
• The Chalukya dynasty was a major power in South India from the 6th to the 12th century CE. 
 
• They were known for their innovative and eclectic architecture, which combined elements of the Dravidian and Nagara styles. 
 
• This hybrid style, known as Vesara, is characterized by its use of **both square and rectangular plans,** as well as its blend of ornate and simple ornamentation.
 
• The Chalukyas were also skilled engineers, and they used their knowledge of mathematics and astronomy to create temples that were both beautiful and structurally sound. 
 
• Some of the most famous examples of Chalukya architecture include the temples at **Aihole, Badami, and Pattadakal. **
 
• These temples are renowned for their intricate carvings, soaring towers, and rich symbolism.
 
• The Chalukyas' use of Vesara architecture was a major contribution to the development of Indian temple architecture. 
 
• Their innovative style helped to pave the way for the later development of the Hoysala and Vijayanagara styles.
 
• Here are some of the features that are characteristic of **Vesara architecture**:
 
 
• ​**A combination of square and rectangular plans**
 
• **A blend of ornate and simple ornamentation**
 
• **The use of pillars with brackets**
 
• **The use of miniature towers on the roof**
 
• **The use of relief sculptures on the walls**
 
• **The use of intricate carvings on the pillars and walls**
 
 
 
• The Vesara style was highly adaptable, and it was used to create a wide variety of temples, including Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist temples. 
 
• 
 
It is a testament to the skill and creativity of the Chalukyas that their temples continue to be admired and studied today.

 

​Therefore the **correct answer is ****Chalukya Dynasty.**
